bodyHtml:
A decision guide to Tsup: what it is for, when it fits, how to start, and which compatibility or maintenance details deserve a closer look.

Quick verdict

Bundle your TypeScript library with no config, powered by esbuild

Shortlist Tsup only if its documented purpose matches your use case; the source signals below are context, not an endorsement.

Best fit — and when to skip it

Tsup is most relevant to developers working with JavaScript/TypeScript. It belongs on a shortlist when that stated purpose matches a concrete requirement.

Skip or postpone it when the documented runtime, license, dependency footprint, or maintenance model conflicts with your project. Popularity alone is not a reason to migrate.

Setup and first checks

Confirm the exact package name, current version, runtime requirement, dependencies, provenance, and release notes before installing tsup in a production project. Start in a disposable example and exercise the use case you actually need.

Maintenance and risk signals

The collected source record shows 7.1M weekly downloads, version 8.5.1, and released 2025-11-12.

The recorded Node.js requirement is >=18.

The current package metadata lists 17 direct dependencies.

The registry lists 2 maintainers.

The source reports the MIT license.

Registry downloads include automated requests and are not unique users, satisfaction, or proof of quality.

Bottom line

Tsup is worth a closer look when its stated purpose and ecosystem fit your project. Compare it with related tools, verify the current documentation, and test the smallest realistic use case before committing.

Try it safely

npm install tsup

Use the official npm package page to confirm the current version, documentation, dependencies, provenance, and compatibility requirements before installing it in an important project.
